trigger: ANY call to MCP tools/list by ANY client, unconditionally
summary: 76b757714's get_execution_children outputSchema literal (mcp_server.cpp:875) is syntactically INVALID JSON: one extra closing brace prematurely closes the tool's enclosing JObj right after the outputSchema value, before result_truncated_by_cap/required are appended. Verified 3 ways: (1) python3 json.loads() on the exact literal -> 'Extra data: line 1 column 364'; (2) empirical reproduction -- an unrelated, later-declared KEK test (test_mcp_server.cpp:15499) fails nlohmann::json::parse on the FULL tools/list body; (3) happy-path traced the actual serialization (JObj::raw() = pure string concatenation, zero validation) and confirmed this is a WHOLE-CATALOGUE discovery outage: every tool declared AFTER get_execution_children in kTools[] becomes structurally unreachable via tools/list for any strict client, not merely this one tool. Mitigating: tools/call's actual invocation-time response for get_execution_children uses an independent fixed sentinel schema (kObjectOutputSchema), so a client bypassing discovery (already knows the tool name) still gets a well-formed response -- discovery-only outage, not invocation-time. consistency-auditor ran a repo-wide sweep of all 285 logical JSON schema documents in mcp_server.cpp (764 raw tokens collapsed across MSVC-C2026-workaround splits) and confirmed this is the ONLY parse failure in the entire tool/prompt table. check-mcp-retry-hints.py and check-api-parity.py both ran clean on this diff but neither covers response-shape/schema-body JSON validity (architect independently confirmed check-api-parity.py is route/tool-EXISTENCE only) -- quality-engineer separately found ZERO transport-level test coverage of result_truncated_by_cap for this tool (qa-2146-a2r1-children-truncation-untested-transports), which is exactly why this shipped undetected by the PR's own new tests. Fix: remove the one extra '}' before ',"result_truncated_by_cap"' so it nests inside 'properties' as a sibling of 'children', matching list_schedules' correct pattern byte-for-byte. MUST ship with a regression test that round-trips json::parse on the actual tools/list response.
classification_rationale: shipped schema is not valid JSON, contradicting A5's typed-output-schema requirement and the MCP JSON-RPC wire contract.

trigger: get_children_checked's SELECT...WHERE parent_id=$1 ORDER BY dispatched_at DESC LIMIT $2 has no supporting index on parent_id; executions/agent_exec_status have no retention sweep of their own so the table grows unboundedly
summary: Confirmed via git show origin/dev: only idx_executions_status/idx_agent_exec_agent/idx_executions_dispatched/idx_executions_definition exist -- no parent_id index ever existed; pre-existing, newly-reachable via 2 new callers (REST v1, MCP) added by this PR. The LIMIT cap+1 fix bounds ROWS RETURNED but not SCAN COST -- Postgres has no efficient plan for parent_id=$1 (Seq Scan, or worst-case near-full-table Index Scan Backward on dispatched_at). Reopens the exact pool-exhaustion axis the original BLOCKING finding was about (pool shared with RbacStore's fail-closed auth). unhappy-path independently corroborated and strengthened with 2 more facts, recorded separately as up-2146-a2r1-index-statement-timeout-missing (same root cause, second reporter, own severity_native). Derives HIGH/BLOCKING per SKILL.md I5(b). Recommend: CREATE INDEX idx_executions_parent ON executions(parent_id) WHERE parent_id <> '' (partial, since parent_id defaults to '' for every non-rerun execution) PLUS a SET LOCAL statement_timeout on this connection.
classification_rationale: the fix's own stated purpose (close the unbounded-query pool-exhaustion risk) is not fully achieved by row-capping alone.

summary: CORRECTION (chaos-injector, Gate 5, verified against server.cpp:4160-4182/pg_pool.hpp:84-89): the 'no statement_timeout at all' framing was imprecise -- pg_pool_ is constructed with PgPool::Options' DEFAULT statement_timeout_ms=30000, injected as a startup GUC on every connection. This bounds a wedged scan to ~30s, not unbounded. However 30s is a pool-WIDE default, not tuned for this hot path, and vastly exceeds the 1500ms kReadTimeout acquire-budget other callers wait on -- so under concurrency a worker/connection can still be pinned ~20x longer than the caller's own timeout budget, starving the pool shared with RbacStore's fail-closed auth (execution_tracker_ and rbac_store_ share the SAME pg_pool_ singleton per server.cpp:5629/5929, confirmed empirically -- blast radius is fleet-wide auth degradation, not execution-history-only). Derived severity HIGH/BLOCKING is UNCHANGED by this correction. Recovery confirmed clean: pg_pool.hpp's Lease RAII unconditionally releases on every return path including degraded/nullopt returns, and release() discards unhealthy connections -- no leak found on the timeout/query-failure paths in these 4 commits; self-heals without manual intervention once PG pressure clears. Recommend: a per-call-site SET LOCAL statement_timeout tuned closer to the caller's own budget, PLUS the index.
classification_rationale: corrects an imprecise trigger description from the prior row while confirming the derived severity and gate outcome are unchanged.
